small_guidance:
- The file has a stray `</old_str_3>` / `<new_str_3>` diff marker embedded in the source between the two kernels, which truncates the `gemm_sigmoid_kernel` body and leaves `def gemm_lse_kernel(` with an unclosed paren. Strip those marker lines so the module is valid Python.
- Keep the autotune configs but make sure `BLOCK_N` in `gemm_lse_kernel` is ≤ N (=1024); a 1024-wide N tile means the inner N loop runs once per M-tile which is fine — just ensure `tl.where(mask_n,...,-inf)` is used before `tl.max` (already done).
- Cache `_w2T` in fp16 only if the sigmoid output is fp16; otherwise match dtypes to avoid an implicit upcast inside `tl.dot`.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as two clean Triton kernels in a single file with no diff/patch markers: (1) tiled GEMM + bias + sigmoid epilogue producing H in fp16, (2) a single persistent kernel per M-tile that streams N-tiles of the second GEMM and folds bias + online logsumexp (running max + running sum, rescale on max update) directly on the accumulator, writing only the final `lse` vector of length M.
- For the LSE kernel, since N=1024 fits, prefer one program per M-tile with `BLOCK_N=1024` (no N loop) and stream only K in `BLOCK_K=64` chunks; this turns the epilogue into a single row-wise reduction with no rescale loop and removes mask logic on N entirely (N is a multiple of 1024).
- Keep weights pre-transposed as buffers in `__init__` so the K dimension is the inner contiguous axis of B; pass biases as plain pointers and load once per N-tile in the epilogue. Do not pre-reduce any weight tensor — every GEMM must execute at runtime.
